Cyber Attack Disrupts Zambia’s Payment Systems, Trade and Daily Life

LUSAKA – Zambia’s financial and commercial sectors have been thrown into turmoil following a widespread cyber attack on the nation’s payments infrastructure, authorities confirmed on Thursday. The incident, which began early Wednesday morning, has crippled electronic transactions across banks, retail outlets, and mobile money platforms, causing ripple effects throughout the economy.

According to the National Cybersecurity Response Centre, the attack targeted critical digital payment processing networks used by banks, mobile operators, and financial service providers. “We are facing an unprecedented assault on the backbone of our payments system,” said Centre spokesperson Judith Mwale. “As of now, electronic transfers and card transactions are severely limited, with many systems offline.”

Major supermarkets in Lusaka and Ndola reported long queues and growing frustration as customers were unable to pay for goods except in cash. “We turned away over 400 customers today who couldn’t pay because their cards would not go through,” said Chipo Banda, manager at the Shopzmart chain.

The Zambia National Chamber of Commerce and Industry warned that the disruption threatens essential supply chains, as wholesalers and transporters rely heavily on digital payments for fuel, goods, and services. “If this continues into the weekend, we could see shortages of basic commodities,” said Chamber president Elijah Mulenga.

Mobile money services, used by millions of Zambians for daily transactions, are also affected. Tech analyst Kelvin Phiri explained, “Many small businesses operate almost entirely through mobile money. The inability to process payments is devastating for them, especially in rural areas.”

Officials have not disclosed the origin of the attack but stated that specialists from Zambian SecurePay and ConnectaBank are working with government teams to restore services. The Ministry of Finance urged calm, advising citizens to carry cash where possible and warning against panic withdrawals.

As of Thursday evening, the majority of digital payment services remained unavailable. The Bank of Zambia confirmed all efforts were being made to restore normal operations but could not give a timeline. The investigation into the attack is ongoing.
